Do distinct groups differ? A heterogeneity test before pooling

Source: R/indigenous_mental_health.R
dstntst.Rd

Tests whether the estimates of one indicator for distinct groups (First Nations, Metis and Inuit; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; any groups with published intervals) differ more than their intervals allow, and says how much of their spread is real: the evidence for reporting each group distinctly rather than as one pooled figure.

Usage

dstntst(
  data,
  grp,
  est,
  lower,
  upper,
  qual = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95,
  pooled = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per group.

grp, est, lower, upper

Column names.

qual

Optional column of quality flags; suppressed rows are left out (see qltyrcd).

conflvl

Confidence level of the published intervals, and the level of the verdict printed (default 0.95).

pooled

Optional labels of rows that pool other groups.

Value

A list of class rmbl_distinctions: groups (the estimates used, with their standard errors), pooled (the inverse-variance mean) and poose, q, df, p_value, i2, leftout (the rows not used) and conflvl. print() and plot() show it.

Details

With estimates \(y_g\), standard errors \(s_g\) from the published intervals and weights \(w_g = 1/s_g^2\), Cochran's \(Q = \sum w_g (y_g - \bar y_w)^2\) has a chi-squared distribution on \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom when the groups share one value, and \(I^2 = \max(0, (Q - (G-1))/Q)\) is the share of the spread that is real rather than sampling error (Higgins and Thompson 2002). A pooled figure is a weighted mean of different populations whenever \(I^2\) is large; the population-weighted total Statistics Canada publishes also depends on how many people are in each group, so it is mostly a First Nations figure where First Nations people are most of the Indigenous population. Rows that pool groups are left out (pooled; see indgap); every other row is included, so drop the reference group (non-Indigenous people) yourself, and never test overlapping groups ("alone" beside “alone or in combination”) together: they are not independent. With two or three groups the test has little power and \(I^2\) is imprecise; a large \(p\) is not evidence that the groups are the same.

References

Higgins JPT, Thompson SG (2002). Quantifying heterogeneity in a meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine 21(11):1539-1558. doi:10.1002/sim.1186

See also

indgap.

Examples

# perceived mental health very good or excellent, 2019/2022, adults (table
# 13-10-0924-01)
h <- indiex("health")
mh <- h[
  h$period == "2019/2022" &
    h$age == "Total, 18 years and over" &
    h$group != "Non-Indigenous" &
    h$indicator == "Perceived mental health, very good or excellent",
]
dt <- dstntst(mh, "group", "estimate", "lower", "upper", qual = "quality")
dt
#> ╭── Distinctions test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Groups       3                                                       │
#> │   Cochran's Q  11.97 on 2 df                                           │
#> │   p-value      0.003                                                   │
#> │   I-squared    83% of the variation is beyond chance                   │
#> │   Pooled       49.11 (se 0.973, inverse-variance mean)                 │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   group          estimate     se  95% CI                               │
#> │   -------------  --------  -----  --------------                       │
#> │   First Nations     45.80  1.429  [43.00, 48.60]                       │
#> │   Métis             52.80  1.454  [49.95, 55.65]                       │
#> │   Inuit             47.80  3.291  [41.35, 54.25]                       │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Q says the groups differ: report each one, not the pooled figure.    │
#> │   Q = 11.97, p = 0.00252.                                              │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Distinctions-based: each group is reported on its own; a             │
#> │   pan-Indigenous total is left out of the test, never used as a group. │
#> │   Higgins and Thompson (2002) for Q and I-squared.                     │
#> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
plot(dt)

# your own table: made-up numbers, with the pooled row named
own <- data.frame(
  group = c("Aboriginal", "Torres Strait Islander", "Both"),
  est = c(24.0, 31.0, 24.6),
  lo = c(22.1, 26.2, 22.8),
  hi = c(25.9, 35.8, 26.4)
)
dstntst(own, "group", "est", "lo", "hi", pooled = "Both")
#> ╭── Distinctions test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Groups       2                                                       │
#> │   Cochran's Q  7.06 on 1 df                                            │
#> │   p-value      0.008                                                   │
#> │   I-squared    86% of the variation is beyond chance                   │
#> │   Pooled       24.95 (se 0.901, inverse-variance mean)                 │
#> │   Left out     Both                                                    │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   group                   estimate     se  95% CI                      │
#> │   ----------------------  --------  -----  --------------              │
#> │   Aboriginal                    24  0.969  [22.10, 25.90]              │
#> │   Torres Strait Islander        31  2.449  [26.20, 35.80]              │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Q says the groups differ: report each one, not the pooled figure.    │
#> │   Q = 7.06, p = 0.00787.                                               │
#> │                                                                        │
#> │   Distinctions-based: each group is reported on its own; a             │
#> │   pan-Indigenous total is left out of the test, never used as a group. │
#> │   Higgins and Thompson (2002) for Q and I-squared.                     │
#> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
